subject.title: Codex app-server client closes before long maintenance turn completes; Gateway restart also terminates active turn without graceful recovery

question: For a Codex-backed turn interrupted by Gateway restart/SIGTERM or app-server client close after possible side effects, should OpenClaw resume the turn, synthesize a final maintenance status, or fail closed with restart-specific guidance?
rationale: The source proves the failure path, but safe recovery depends on replay safety and whether partially executed maintenance work may be retried, summarized, or only reported as interrupted.

options.title: Define restart-aware recovery contract
options.body: Treat Gateway shutdown and unexpected app-server close as distinct outcomes, retry only replay-safe turns, and emit a durable channel follow-up for interrupted maintenance work.

options.title: Improve diagnostics only
options.body: Keep fail-closed behavior but replace the generic app-server copy with restart/client-close specific guidance and logging triggers.

options.title: Wait for live repro
options.body: Keep the issue open without implementation until maintainers capture a current-main live reproduction of the long maintenance and restart sequence.

recommendation.title: Define restart-aware recovery contract
recommendation.body: Treat Gateway shutdown and unexpected app-server close as distinct outcomes, retry only replay-safe turns, and emit a durable channel follow-up for interrupted maintenance work.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the clearest current-history owner across the touched close, reply, retry, and Gateway shutdown surfaces.
